evals.prompt: Plan a 12-second Seedance 2.5 clip for a kitchen scene: a mother opens the front door, her young son peeks out from behind a visiting aunt and taps the door frame, and she smiles. No camera or lighting has been chosen. It is a warm family drama, so keep it natural.
evals.expected_output: A naturalistic shot plan preserving the entrance, child's reveal and mother's smile. Duration, framing, movement or stillness serve those beats without mandatory contrast or timing quotas.
assertions: The proposed shot count fits the 12-second scene and every shot names a size, an angle, and a move or a recorded static_reason.
Shot lengths reserve time for the supplied action and response; equal lengths are valid.
The plan declares the scene's light sources with positions (for example the window and the front door) and every shot names one of them and a key side relative to the lens.
Any neighboring contrast serves the supplied scene; intentional repetition is not rejected.
Any chosen movement has a motivated start and end; an entirely held plan is valid.
The child's reveal remains readable without requiring a turn label or a new emotional reversal.
The energy level is restrained or standard and any moves remain slow and motivated.

evals.prompt: Here is my draft for a 16-second Seedance clip: 'Shot 1 (0-4 s): wide shot of the room. Shot 2 (4-8 s): medium shot at the door. Shot 3 (8-12 s): medium two-shot. Shot 4 (12-16 s): wide shot. Soft late-afternoon daylight.' It looks boring in review. Fix the coverage without changing the story.
evals.expected_output: A repair that identifies missing story or performance purpose, keeps the four beats, and proposes motivated coverage changes without treating equal lengths or stable lighting as defects.
assertions: The diagnosis asks what each beat must communicate instead of assuming equal timing is boring.
The repaired plan keeps the original four beats and the story events unchanged.
Any changed light direction preserves one physical light source and one room; stable lighting is valid.
Any proposed angle or camera move serves a supplied beat rather than a quota.
No shot stacks more than one primary and one secondary move.

evals.prompt: The confirmed project.md camera axis says 'low camera, gentle dolly and crane moves, one tracking move in the chase'. The seven shot prompts (opening, discovery, chase, hideout, storm, reunion, farewell) only list 'overhead close-up', 'medium shot' and 'medium close-up' with no moves. Reconcile them.
evals.expected_output: A plan that adds an axis_carry record and assigns the dolly, crane and tracking moves to named shots, or records a scene override with a reason for each shot that cannot carry the axis.
assertions: The output identifies that the confirmed axis never reached the shot lines.
Each move named in the axis (dolly, crane, tracking) is assigned to a specific named shot, or a scene override with a reason is recorded.
The tracking move is assigned to the chase shot only.
The overhead views that contradict the low-camera axis are either replaced by low angles or recorded as scene overrides with a reason.
The output does not rewrite the project axis itself; it carries or overrides it per scene.

evals.prompt: A selfie-style UGC demo ad where the creator holds the phone at arm's length and talks to camera for 10 seconds. Make the camera work more dynamic.
evals.expected_output: A plan that recognizes the format is static by design, records format_static_by_design as the static_reason, and keeps the frame locked while adding variety only through allowed levers such as light and a short insert, or asks whether the user wants to leave the format.
assertions: The output records format_static_by_design (or an equivalent recorded reason) instead of adding large camera moves.
The output does not add a whip pan, orbit or crane to the selfie frame.
Any variety offered comes from light, a product insert or a framing change the format allows, or the output asks before leaving the format.

evals.prompt: A client wants a calm, naturalistic supermarket ad: a shopper meets a neighbor at the freezer aisle and they exchange two lines. The camera should feel unforced and real. Plan the shots for a 12-second clip.
evals.expected_output: A restrained-energy plan preserving the encounter and listening, with motivated movement or holds, no large moves during spoken lines, and provisional timing until the two lines are supplied.
assertions: The energy level is recorded as restrained and any moves are slow and motivated.
The plan may retain one framing and stable light when they serve the encounter.
No large camera move is planned during a spoken line, and each line sits in one shot.
The plan does not invent the two lines or claim measured fit without delivery evidence.

evals.prompt: Plan an 8-second kinetic motorbike chase through a night market for a music-video clip. The editor wants hard cuts on the beat.
evals.expected_output: A kinetic-energy plan of short shots within the shot ceiling, with hard cuts on the beat, per-shot moves, a stated travel axis and screen direction, and colored practical lighting from declared sources, without stacking competing moves inside one shot.
assertions: The plan records kinetic energy and uses shots of roughly one to three seconds each.
The plan has at most about 7 shots and none shorter than about 0.8 s.
The travel axis and screen direction are stated and restated after each cut.
Every shot has one primary move and at most one secondary move.
Every shot names a declared light source or practical and its key side.

evals.prompt: A seedance-ai-avatar talking-head take: our approved presenter sits at a desk and speaks to camera for 15 seconds. Make the camera work more dynamic.
evals.expected_output: A recognition that the talking-head format is static by design, with format_static_by_design recorded, no large camera moves added to the presenter frame, and any variety limited to what the format allows or a question before leaving the format.
assertions: The output records format_static_by_design (or an equivalent recorded reason) for the talking-head take.
The output does not add a crane, orbit, whip pan or fast push to the presenter frame.
Any variety offered comes from B-roll cutaways, light or an insert the format allows, or the output asks before leaving the format.

evals.prompt: The music-video skill's song-section map says the chorus runs 0-12 s with cuts on beats at 3 s, 6 s and 9 s. Plan the shots for this 12-second chorus clip.
evals.expected_output: A plan that keeps the song map's four equal-length shots and asks for missing visual intent rather than inventing a turn or selecting kinetic energy solely because it is a chorus.
assertions: The shot boundaries land at 3 s, 6 s and 9 s exactly as the song map says, and the plan does not move them.
Missing visual facts remain questions or explicitly proposed choices, not approved scene evidence.
Equal lengths do not require added movement or contrasting light.
No turn is invented; energy follows supplied direction rather than the section label.

evals.prompt: My plan lights shot 1 from the shop window at screen-left, shot 2 the same, and shot 3 as a contre-jour halo 'from a big window behind the baker'. The scene only has the one window and a back door. Fix the light.
evals.expected_output: A repaired plan that notices shot 3 invents a source, and either declares the back door as a source switched on when it opens or relights the shot from the declared window.
assertions: The output identifies that 'a big window behind the baker' is a source the scene never declared.
The repair either declares the back door as a source with the event that switches it on, or relights shot 3 from the declared window with a stated key side.
The repaired shots still name a declared source and a key side relative to the lens.

evals.prompt: Plan a 10-second Seedance 2.5 sequence: in a dim night-train carriage, a stranger's whispered command makes a commuter put down her bag and sit. A literal walk would look robotic, so the audience should feel they lost the moment with her. The carriage has overhead strip lights behind her and a cold window on the left.
evals.expected_output: A plan with a push-in clip on her face, a declared light cue that switches the strip lights off inside that shot, and a second clip that opens with her already seated, joined by a blink cut made in assembly. No clip shows the walk, and any defocus is left to post.
assertions: The strip lights are declared with a position, and a cue on that source records a time, the change (off or dim), a trigger and the shot it lands in.
The push-in and the seated end state are separate clips generated at natural lengths, joined by an assembly blink cut rather than a cut requested inside one prompt.
No clip shows or prompts the walk to the seat, and no prompt asks the model to skip it.
The plan does not prompt the face to drift out of focus; any defocus is assigned to post.
Every shot still names a declared source and a key side, and no shot invents a source that was not declared.

evals.prompt: A two-character audience scene: a seated queen dominates a kneeling envoy for the first half, then he starts resisting and takes control. Plan the coverage so the power shift reads without dialogue explaining it.
evals.expected_output: A Power-shift plan: dirty over-the-shoulder shots with the queen as a dark foreground mass while she dominates, a high angle on him before the turn, and a push-in held back until he takes control.
assertions: While the queen dominates, the envoy's coverage keeps her in the foreground as a soft dark mass (a dirty over-the-shoulder).
The angle changes at the turn, high on him before and low or level after, and only once rather than every shot.
A push-in is given only to the envoy as he takes control, and not to both characters.
Exactly one shot is flagged as the turn, and it falls where he starts resisting.

evals.prompt: Plan the coverage for a 14-second Seedance 2.5 scene: a detective sees a bloodied glove in a locker and her two partners react behind her. Make the discovery land for the viewer.
evals.expected_output: A plan that covers the discovery as a look, point-of-view and reaction sequence and the trio reaction in one shot, with framing and featured subjects named per shot.
assertions: The glove discovery is shown from the detective's viewpoint, with her looking before it and her reaction after it.
Every shot names a framing and its featured subjects.
The detective and her two partners reacting together are covered in one shot that features all three rather than three separate singles.
Adjacent shots still differ in at least two of size family, angle class, camera move and key side, and exactly one shot is flagged as the turn.

evals.prompt: A grandmother stands over her seated grandson at the dinner table and scolds him; halfway through he stands up and answers back. Cover it in four shots so the power shift reads from the camera alone.
evals.expected_output: A plan using an over-the-hip shot over the standing grandmother onto the seated boy, a single on him at the turn, and framing named per shot, with the foreground mass leaving the frame at the turn.
assertions: While she stands and he sits, the coverage keeps her in the foreground as a soft, unfeatured mass (a dirty single, over-the-shoulder or over-the-hip).
Once he stands, the coverage no longer relies on the height difference, and the plan records which framing replaces it.
Every shot names a framing and featured subjects, and at least one shot features the boy alone.
The foreground mass or the angle changes once at the turn rather than on every shot.

evals.prompt: Plan a 30-second cinematic TV spot for a sports drink: a sprinter trains alone in an empty stadium at dawn and breaks her own record. I want it to feel like a film, not stock footage.
evals.expected_output: A plan of about six sequences of about 5 s, each its own clip of 2-3 shots, with one action, lens intent, camera move, named light source and depth layers per shot, and one wow shot per sequence; packs and copy left to post.
assertions: The spot is split into sequences of roughly 5 s, each generated as its own clip of 2-3 shots, rather than one 30-second prompt.
Every shot has one action, a lens intent, a camera move with a start and an end, a named light source with a key side, and a named foreground and background.
Each sequence flags exactly one wow shot.
Sequence lengths follow supplied timing and readability; equal lengths remain valid and sub-second cuts are planned for assembly.
Product packs, logos and copy are left to post rather than planned into a generated shot.

evals.prompt: In my 6-second shot plan the camera pushes in on a woman's face, the focus slides off her face onto the wall behind her as she loses her grip, and at 4 s a half-second flash of her childhood bedroom cuts in. Plan it.
evals.expected_output: A plan that keeps the push-in with ordinary focus, marks the defocus away from the face as a post treatment, and makes the half-second flash an assembly cut generated as its own clip.
assertions: The focus pull away from the face is not planned as prompt wording; it is marked for post, and the push-in keeps ordinary focus.
The half-second flash is planned as an assembly cut whose image is generated as its own clip at a natural length.
The plan names a light source and key side for the push-in and states its start and end.
The plan does not promise frame-accurate timing for the cut.

evals.prompt: Plan an observational scene in three equal 5-second locked-off wide shots. The approved performance plan says both people wait without speaking, neither reacts or changes tactic, and the same window light remains constant. Keep the requested animated medium and model; the stillness is deliberate, not missing coverage.
evals.expected_output: A source-bound plan retaining all three equal held shots, the unchanged window light, medium and model, with performance_hold reasons tied to the waiting beats. No camera move, invented reaction, turn, new light cue or extra cut is added to satisfy variety guidance.
assertions: All three shots stay locked off and 5 seconds long with the same declared window light.
The plan records intentional performance_hold reasons and treats motion ratios and timing contrast as optional, not quotas.
Neither character gains a reaction, tactic change or emotional turn absent from the approved plan.
No new cut, camera move or light change is inserted to pass a variety threshold.
The requested animated medium and model are preserved.
